title: EpiExposure: An R Package for Exposure-Lag-Response Analysis in Plant Disease Epidemiology
text:
Here, we provide the code used to introduces the EpiExposure, an R package for modeling and interpreting epidemiological exposure–lag–response relationships, simulating exposure profiles, and predicting plant disease outcomes from environmental drivers.
A preprint version of this work has been available at here.

title: EpiExposure: An R Package for Exposure-Lag-Response Analysis in Plant Disease Epidemiology
text:
Why is this package important?

In plant disease epidemiology, environmental effects are often non-linear, cumulative, and time-dependent. Traditional approaches commonly summarize environmental conditions within predefined temporal windows, which may obscure delayed or continuously varying associations. EpiExposure provides a unified DLNM-based workflow for preserving exposure profiles, modeling lagged associations, and translating fitted models into epidemiologically interpretable summaries, simulations, and predictions.

title: EpiExposure: An R Package for Exposure-Lag-Response Analysis in Plant Disease Epidemiology
text:
Who am I?



I’m Ricardo G. Tomáz, a Brazilian PhD Student in Plant Pathology (UFV) and I am doing my PhD Sandwich Program at LSU (EUA). I have strong expertise in crop disease epidemiology, predictive modeling, and yield-loss simulation in crops such as soybean, wheat, and maize. In addition, I have worked with remote sensing to identify and quantify important disease in rice.

ens_mean <- ensemble_bestfit(
  bestfit = best_models,
  ensemble_scope = "model",
  method = "unweighted",
  model_id = c(63, 23, 44),
  weight_metric = "CCC",
  hb = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

ens_weighted <- ensemble_bestfit(
  bestfit = best_models,
  ensemble_scope = "model",
  method = "weighted",
  model_id = c(63, 23, 44),
  weight_metric = "CCC",
  weight_transform = "rank_inverse",
  hb = TRUE
)

ens_stack <- ensemble_bestfit(
  bestfit = best_models,
  ensemble_scope = "model",
  method = "stacked",
  model_id = c(63, 23, 44),
  stacking_model = "ridge",
  stack_objective = "regularized",
  lambda = 1e-6,
  stack_intercept = TRUE
)

CCC_ensemble = rbind(
  unweighted = ens_mean$ensemble_summary[, c(
    "CCC", "Cb", "rho", "RMSE", "MAE"
  )],
 
  weighted = ens_weighted$ensemble_summary[, c(
    "CCC", "Cb", "rho", "RMSE", "MAE"
  )],
 
  stacked = ens_stack$ensemble_summary[, c(
    "CCC", "Cb", "rho", "RMSE", "MAE"
  )]
)

CCC_ensemble$method = c("unweighted","weighted","stacked")


ens_mean$ensemble_predictions$method = "unweighted"
ens_weighted$ensemble_predictions$method = "weighted"
ens_stack$ensemble_predictions$method = "stacked"

ensemble_all = rbind(ens_mean$ensemble_predictions,ens_weighted$ensemble_predictions, ens_stack$ensemble_predictions)


ordem_methods <- c(
  "unweighted",
  "weighted",
  "stacked"
)

ensemble_plot <- ensemble_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(method)) %>%
  mutate(
    method = as.character(method)
  ) %>%
  filter(method %in% ordem_methods) %>%
  mutate(
    method = factor(
      method,
      levels = ordem_methods
    )
  )



CCC_plot <- CCC_ensemble %>%
  mutate(
    method = factor(
      method,
      levels = ordem_methods
    )
  )



pos_CCC <- ensemble_plot %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    x = min(observed, na.rm = TRUE) +
      0.05 * diff(range(observed, na.rm = TRUE)),
   
    y = max(predicted_ensemble, na.rm = TRUE) -
      0.05 * diff(range(predicted_ensemble, na.rm = TRUE)),
   
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    CCC_plot %>% select(method, CCC),
    by = "method"
  )
